0. Input

Program:

for (int i = 1; i <= 2; i++) {
    for (int j = 1; j <= 3; j++) {
        System.out.println(i + " " + j);
    }
}

Question: In what order are the lines printed, and how many are there?

System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterLoopHeader | wrong rule: Puts a ; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:for_loop->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:for_loop->ForIsConditional | wrong rule: The body of a for statement executes at most once. | right rule: The body of a for statement runs once for every pass on which the condition is true, which can be many times. | | mis:for_loop->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:for_loop->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:for_loop->ForWhileNotInterchangeable | wrong rule: Some loops can only be written with for, others only with while. | right rule: Any for loop can be rewritten as a while loop and vice versa; for just packages init, test and update. | | mis:for_loop->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:for_loop->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:for_loop->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:for_loop->LoopImpliedByOneTest | wrong rule: Testing one case is enough; Java will repeat the test for the other values by itself. | right rule: A statement runs once each time control reaches it; repeating a test for many values needs a loop. | | mis:for_loop->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:for_loop->MissingBraces | wrong rule: Omits braces around a single-statement body of if, for or while. | right rule: Braces are optional for a single-statement body, but using them anyway avoids bugs when statements are added later. | | mis:for_loop->ProgramEndsAfterLoop | wrong rule: When a loop finishes the program ends, so code after the loop never runs. | right rule: When the loop condition becomes false, control continues with the first statement after the loop. | | mis:for_loop->ReturnDoesNotExitLoop | wrong rule: A return inside a loop does not end the loop; it sets a value each pass (the last one is returned) or returns several values. | right rule: When return executes, the method ends at once, so the loop stops on that pass. | | mis:for_loop->SingleIterationInsteadOfLoop | wrong rule: A task that must be repeated is written once, without a loop, as if one pass were enough. | right rule: A step that must happen several times (or an unknown number of times) needs a loop such as while or for; ; ) { }, with the three parts separated by semicolons; it is, with only a few exceptions, equivalent to ; while () { ; }. | | lvl:for_loop@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: Run the initializer once; i < N; i++) gives i each valid index 0..N-1 exactly once in increasing order, the standard way to process every array element. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#3 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A simulation runs a fixed number of trials with an outer for loop (for (int t = 0; t < T; t++)), each trial simulated inside the body. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#4 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: In a for loop, continue skips the rest of the body and transfers control directly to the increment, then the next test; this is one of the few places where the for/while equivalence fails. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#5 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A variable declared in the for header is in scope only in the header and the body, so it cannot be used after the loop. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#6 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A fencepost loop is a for loop that handles one item (the first or last) outside the loop so that separators come out n-1 times for n items. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#7 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A flag search loop is a for loop that sets a boolean flag when some pass finds the target and leaves it set afterwards; Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:control_flow->CodeAfterIfSkipped | wrong rule: When the then branch runs, the code after the if is skipped. | right rule: After the if finishes, execution continues with the next statement either way. | | mis:control_flow->FalseConditionRestartsProgram | wrong rule: When an if condition is false (and there is no else), control jumps back to the start of the program. | right rule: A false condition skips the then branch and execution continues with the statement after the if statement. | | mis:control_flow->FalseLoopRepeatsNextCode | wrong rule: A loop is an iterative if-else: while the condition is true the body repeats, and when it is false the code after the loop repeats. | right rule: Only the body is repeated; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:control_flow->IfConditionWatched | wrong rule: An if statement watches its condition while the program runs and fires as soon as the condition becomes true (if = whenever). | right rule: An if condition is tested once, when control reaches the if statement; later changes to the variables do not trigger the branch. | | mis:control_flow->IfWaitsForCondition | wrong rule: An IF statement earlier in the program stays active and fires later, e.g. inside a later loop, when its condition becomes true. | right rule: An if is evaluated once when control reaches it; afterwards it is inactive unless control returns to it. | | mis:control_flow->LoopImpliedByOneTest | wrong rule: Testing one case is enough; Java will repeat the test for the other values by itself. | right rule: A statement runs once each time control reaches it; repeating a test for many values needs a loop. | | mis:control_flow->NoShortCircuit | wrong rule: logical AND/OR always evaluate both sides (Java short-circuits them) | right rule: In p && q, q is evaluated only when p is true; in p || q, q is evaluated only when p is false. | | mis:control_flow->ProgramEndsAfterLoop | wrong rule: When a loop finishes the program ends, so code after the loop never runs. | right rule: When the loop condition becomes false, control continues with the first statement after the loop. | | mis:control_flow->ProgramLooksAhead | wrong rule: The program knows or sees what later lines will do and acts on those goals at the current line, e.g. it stops 'at ten' because it wants to draw a box. | right rule: Each statement executes using only the current state; later lines have no effect until control reaches them. | | mis:control_flow->ReturnDoesNotExitLoop | wrong rule: A return inside a loop does not end the loop; it sets a value each pass (the last one is returned) or returns several values. | right rule: When return executes, the method ends at once, so the loop stops on that pass. | | mis:control_flow->StatementsRunInAnyOrder | wrong rule: Statements in a program can run in any order. | right rule: Without control statements, statements run once each, top to bottom. |

(here mixing in: "Statements in a program can run in any order") | | lvl:control_flow@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: Control flow is the order in which a program's statements are executed (statement sequencing); conditionals and loops are the statements that change it. | | lvl:control_flow@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: Without control statements every statement executes once, in the order given; a block executes its statements in order from first to last; if/if-else choose between one or two alternatives and loops repeat statements depending on a condition. | | lvl:control_flow@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: Execute the statement at the current point; when it completes normally, control passes to the next statement in the block. println, misconceptions: 6 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:println->PrintWithoutFinalNewline | wrong rule: Ends the output with print and expects it to appear right away. | right rule: Finish a line of print calls with println; some systems hold print output until a newline is printed. | | mis:println->IdentifierCaseInsensitive | wrong rule: System.out.Println and System.out.println name the same method. | right rule: Java is case-sensitive: names of variables, methods and classes that differ only in capitalization are different names. | | mis:println->ParenthesesOnlyIfArgument | wrong rule: println with nothing to print can be written System.out.println; without the parentheses. | right rule: A method call always needs parentheses, so an empty line is printed with System.out.println();. | | mis:println->PrintEqualsPrintln | wrong rule: print and println do the same thing, so print(s1); print(s2); puts s1 and s2 on separate lines. | right rule: println ends the line after printing and print does not, so print(s1); print(s2); puts s1 and s2 on the same line. | | mis:println->PrintNewLineFirst | wrong rule: println(s) prints a newline and then s. | right rule: println(s) prints s and then the newline. | | mis:println->PrintedTextIsExecuted | wrong rule: System.out.println("x is 5"); sets x to 5 (text inside the quotes is run as code). | right rule: Characters inside double quotes are printed literally; println only displays them and changes no variable. Only an assignment such as x = 5; sets x. |

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:nested_loops->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | mis:nested_loops->EmptyInnerLoopSkipsRest | wrong rule: If the inner loop runs zero times, the rest of that outer pass is skipped too. | right rule: An inner loop that runs zero times just ends; the statements after it in the outer body still run. | | mis:nested_loops->InconsistentIndentation | wrong rule: Indents nested blocks inconsistently, so the visual nesting differs from the real nesting. | right rule: Indent consistently, one level deeper for each nested block, so the layout shows the real nesting; the compiler ignores indentation. | | mis:nested_loops->InnerCounterOverwritesOuter | wrong rule: The inner loop count replaces the outer loop count, so the nested loops run as one loop. | right rule: The two counts multiply: the inner body runs (outer passes) x (inner passes) times. | | mis:nested_loops->InnerOuterSwapped | wrong rule: The inner loop's variable changes more slowly than the outer loop's. | right rule: The inner loop runs all its passes for each single pass of the outer loop. | | mis:nested_loops->NestedLoopsLockstep | wrong rule: Nested loops run in step as one loop: both variables change together and both conditions are tested together. | right rule: For each pass of the outer loop the inner loop runs all its passes; the inner variable changes fastest. | | mis:nested_loops->NestedLoopsSequential | wrong rule: The outer loop runs completely, then the inner loop runs completely. | right rule: The inner loop runs all its passes during each single pass of the outer loop. | | mis:nested_loops->OuterLoopIgnored | wrong rule: In nested loops only the inner loop repeats; the outer loop runs once. | right rule: The outer loop repeats as its own condition says, and the inner loop runs fully on each outer pass. |

every needed step and value must be written. | | mis:loop_body->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:loop_body->IfInLoopUnchecked | wrong rule: An if inside a loop body runs its branch on every pass without testing its condition. | right rule: The if condition is tested again on every pass, with the current values, so the branch runs only on passes where it is true. | | mis:loop_body->LoopBodyAlwaysOnce | wrong rule: The loop body always runs at least once, even if the condition is false at the start. | right rule: A while or for body runs zero times when the condition is false at the start. | | mis:loop_body->LoopBodyStatementOutsideLoop | wrong rule: Some statements inside the braces of a loop body are not repeated; they run once, before or after the loop. | right rule: Every statement inside the loop braces is part of the body and runs on every pass. | | mis:loop_body->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:loop_body->LoopOutputSameEachPass | wrong rule: A loop prints the same thing on every pass; the changing loop variable does not affect what the body does. | right rule: The body uses the current value of the loop variable, so its output can differ on each pass. | | mis:loop_body->LoopRunsStatementsSeparately | wrong rule: A loop runs its first body statement all N times, then its second body statement all N times. | right rule: Each pass runs the whole body in order, so the body statements interleave: S1, S2, S1, S2, ... | | mis:loop_body->StateChangeIgnoredAcrossPasses | wrong rule: Values changed by one pass of a loop (other than the loop variable) do not affect later passes. | right rule: Each pass starts from the state left by the previous pass, so a change in one pass carries into the next ones. | | mis:loop_body->StatementAfterLoopInBody | wrong rule: A statement written after the loop is repeated with the loop body. | right rule: The body ends at the closing brace (or after its single statement); code after it runs once, after the loop ends. | | mis:loop_body->WhileStopsMidBody | wrong rule: The loop stops the moment the condition becomes false, even in the middle of the body. | right rule: The condition is tested only before each pass, so the whole body finishes before the loop can stop. |
